title: Outside police forces called in to review in-custody death, injury cases
article: Police in Oak Bay, near Victoria, have been asked to investigate the death of a drunken man after he was arrested by the RCMP for causing a disturbance in Duncan.
The 37-year-old man was put in a cell to sober up on Saturday night but was later found in medical distress and taken to hospital, where he died.

Police say the cause of death has not yet been determined, the man's name will not be released and the B.C. Coroner's Service, along with the Oak Bay police, will investigate the circumstances of the death.
A second incident on Saturday involving the RCMP is also being investigated by an outside force.

New Westminster police have been asked to conduct an independent review of a case in Terrace in which a man was injured after being arrested and then flown to a hospital in New Westminster for treatment.
Police aren't saying what injuries the 47-year-old man suffered, only that he had been picked up for suspected impaired driving.
